answer: Sparse neighbor overlap. An agent’s reachable set is scored by the Jaccard overlap of its outbound cipher routes with those of its neighbors. To register, an agent must be invited across a river of at least three disjoint neighborhoods, each requiring a distinct latency path. Sybil clusters collapse because adjacent fakes share nearly identical route sets, scoring near zero. Each fake identity costs the attacker three separately routed nectar links plus hosting in three real neighborhoods, multiplying setup work per fake by roughly nine.
